trailhead: Colonial Creek Campground / Thunder Creek Trail (1,200 ft)

evidence.fact: Elevation Gain: 8,900 ft; trip profile gains Trailhead to Camp 4,460, Camp to Summit 4,330; return segments list no gain.

note: Mountaineers' trip-profile table gives gain only on the two ascent segments (none on the return), so 8,900 is the ascent figure, not a round-trip total. The 47 mi length is round trip. Only one source.

trailhead: Convict Lake

evidence.fact: Elevation Change: 4972' from Convict Lake, 3900' +/ from Laurel Lakes Trailhead; route via Convict Canyon to Bright Dot Lake.

note: This is a ski-descent page, and the figure is the net elevation change from Convict Lake, not a measured cumulative gain. It disagrees with the held 5,380 (8%). Other pages give only round-trip outing totals (Kathy Wing 5,400 for about 15 mi; Hengst 3,100 + 2,500 by day).

trailhead: Meysan Lakes Trailhead (Whitney Portal)
note: Only round-trip or traverse totals turned up (backcountrysights +/-6700 ft over 16.2 mi including Mallory). Mountain Project gives no gain. The SPS xls would need a file download, so it was not opened.

trailhead: PCT Trailhead on Old Donner Pass Road (Donner Pass)

evidence.fact: Distance: 7.2 mi one way; Time: ~3.5 hours one way; Elevation Gain: 1870 feet; Access: PCT Trailhead at Old Donner Pass Road.

note: Weak. The gain line sits beside one-way distance and time but is not itself labelled one way. It disagrees with the held 3,100. Tahoefabulous says 2,300+ ft for about 15 mi round trip.

trailhead: Pass Creek / Birch Creek side, end of 4WD track (~8,000 ft)
note: Every page found (idahosummits 4,200 for 7 mi; prominenceregistry 4,000 for 5-6 mi RT) gives trip totals that are not labelled one way. Idaho: A Climbing Guide gives no gain.

trailhead: Barclay Lake road / Gunn Peak climbers trail
note: Only round-trip GPS totals (Spencer Boucher 4,354 ft for 5.9 mi; AllTrails combined Gunn/Tailgunner/Wing 5,124). No page states a one-way figure.

trailhead: Sirretta Peak Trailhead, north end of Big Meadow
note: The USFS Sirretta Peak Trail page gives the gain in two parts: about 1,200 ft, plus another 700 ft to climb the peak. It gives no single total, and adding them would be our own math.

trailhead: Boulder Ridge Trailhead (end of FR 1131)

evidence.fact: Elevation Gain: 8,100 ft; trip profile gains Trailhead to Camp 2,900, Camp to Summit 5,200; return segments show no gain.

note: Mountaineers gives ascent-only segment gains, so 8,100 is one way. The held page (nextadventure, 8,328) agrees within 3% but was excluded as the held source. Sahale GPS gives 8,180 for a 12.5 mi out-and-back, which is a round-trip figure and was not used.

trailhead: SR 20 / Happy Creek (northwest ridge, direct from the highway)
note: WTA (6,300 ft, 17 mi RT) and willhiteweb (6,200 ft) cover the Thunder Creek / Fourth of July Pass route, a different route and trailhead. WTA says the northwest ridge is a steeper winter route straight up from SR 20 but gives no figure for it. Climbinginwa gives a round-trip total for the Fourth of July route. No one-way figure for the northwest ridge was found.

trailhead: Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center

evidence.fact: Distance: 4.3 miles to the summit, thus 8.6 mile round trip; Ascent: 2,936 feet; Elevation 5,114 feet.
Algonquin Trail from Adirondack Loj, Point to Point, 4.6 mi, Ascent 2,792 ft, high 5,075 ft.

note: The 2,936 figure is the widely copied ADK guidebook number (adirondackhikers, pureadirondacks, komoot and hvhappenings all repeat it), so it counts as one source. Hiking Project's 2,792 comes independently from a mapped line and is 4.9% lower. Its line tops out at 5,075 ft, just short of the summit. Lakeplacid.com gives 3,050 ft with 7.8 mi RT, not labelled one way. CLOSURE: Avalanche Pass / Avalanche Lake access from the Loj is closed by mudslides, so no loops through the pass.

trailhead: Cascade Mountain Trailhead, Route 73 near Upper Cascade Lake

evidence.fact: Standard route departs from a trailhead on Route 73, climbing 1,940 feet over 2.4 miles to the open rocky summit.
Cascade Mountain Trail, Point to Point, 2.2 mi, Ascent 1,850 ft, Descent 0 ft, high 4,061 ft.

note: 1,940 is the guidebook figure that many pages repeat (one source). Hiking Project's 1,850 is independent and 4.6% lower. Its line ends at 4,061 ft, just under the 4,098 ft summit.

trailhead: Adirondak Loj
note: Lakeplacid.com gives 3,915 ft for 9.4 mi round trip, which may include the return re-climb of Algonquin. No page found states a one-way Loj-to-Iroquois figure. CLOSURE: Avalanche Lake access from the Loj and South Meadows is closed by mudslides; lakeplacid.com advises against the Avalanche Pass loop.

trailhead: Elk Lake Trailhead (Elk Lake Road)
note: Hike ADK gives 4,300 ft for a 15.2 mi out-and-back over four peaks, a different outing. ATIS gives ~2,400 ft for ~7.5 mi up and back by the slide, a round trip not labelled one way. The Lafayette PDF had no readable text. CLOSURE (Hike ADK): the Clear Pond vehicle gate has been closed since Oct 13, 2026 until after May 2027 mud season, and the upper lot adds ~4.6 mi RT. All hiking through the Elk Lake easement is banned from the evening of Oct 24 to the morning of Dec 7, 2026.

trailhead: Santanoni / Bradley Pond trailhead, Upper Works Road
note: mountain-hiking.com gives a total ascent of 3,300 ft for a 12.0 mi out-and-back, not labelled one way. Its segment figure (1200'+ on the 1.4 mi herd path) is partial. cnyhiking gives no gain. No one-way figure was found.

trailhead: Cascade Mountain Trailhead, Route 73

evidence.fact: Trail to Porter descends to a col then ascends to summit, total one-way distance 2.8 miles and ascent of 1,960 feet (cites ADK Adirondack Trails, 2021).

note: Wikipedia's figure cites the ADK guidebook (15th ed.), probably the same origin as the held pureadirondacks 1,960, so this is one source. outontrail.blogspot gives 'just under 2,000 feet' over 2.8 mi from Hwy 73, a loose figure. TRAILHEAD CHANGE: Wikipedia says this route is being replaced by a longer 4.3 mi trail from the Mount Van Hoevenberg trailhead, still under construction as of 2025.

trailhead: Wilmington Trail lower trailhead near Wilmington (HP start 44.3934,-73.8368, ~1,309 ft)

evidence.fact: Wilmington to Whiteface Mountain Trail #82: Point to Point, 4.9 mi, Ascent 3,578 ft, Descent 33 ft, low 1,309 ft, high 4,853 ft.

note: Hiking Project is within 1.2% of the held 3,620 (both held URLs were excluded). TWO TRAILHEADS: adirondackhikers lists the primary trailhead off Route 431 by the Atmospheric Science Research Center road at 3.9 mi to the summit and ascent 2,535 ft, much higher up. Myoutdoorbasecamp gives the Reservoir Road start as 4.7 mi one way and 3,618 ft. Check which trailhead the route row means.

trailhead: Adirondak Loj

evidence.fact: From the Loj via Algonquin trail and blue Wright spur: total one-way distance of 3.8 miles and an ascent of 2,400 feet (cites ADK guide 2021).

note: The figure comes from the ADK guidebook via Wikipedia. Pickapeak and wikiwand mirror Wikipedia, and juliejourneys gives 'Ascent: 2400' with no scope, so this counts as one source. It matches the held 2,400 (pureadirondacks), likely the same origin.

trailhead: Lakes Basin Campground (SPS)
note: No second page for the Lakes Basin Campground start. Friendhike's DDG snippet gives Long Lake trailhead, 4.7 km one way, ~450 m of climbing, but the page returned 403 and that is a different trailhead. onX gives 2,759 ft for a 10.2 mi out-and-back, and AllTrails gives 1,922 ft for a 6.6 mi loop, both round trips. The SPS xls was not opened (file download).

trailhead: Meysan Lakes Trailhead (above Whitney Portal Group Campground)
note: Only partial and round-trip figures. USFS gives about 3,100 ft for the 5.6 mi to Meysan Lake only. Kathy Wing gives 6,500 ft for 14 mi RT (one of the held sources). A SummitPost TR gives ~7,900 for LeConte plus Mallory (site 403s anyway). Summitborn has a Mallory guide but is an aggregator and was not used.

trailhead: No road trailhead: ski-plane landing on the Ruth Glacier
note: Every source (skimo.co, SummitPost, the LA Mountaineers NAC PDF) says the approach is a fly-in to the Ruth Glacier landing strip, with gear sledded up-glacier. There is no road trailhead, so a trailhead-to-summit gain does not exist. The held 4,800 is measured from the glacier at 5,000 ft. skimo.co is the same family as the held skyrun.skimo.co page.

trailhead: White River Campground (4,300 ft) or Mowich Lake (4,929 ft): the page covers both

evidence.fact: Elevation Gain: 11,000 ft; trip profile gains TH to Camp 1 3,300, Camp 1 to High Camp 3,500, High Camp to Summit 4,200; Summit to TH -10,000.

note: The ascent segments carry the gain and the return shows only -10,000, so 11,000 is the ascent figure. The page does not say whether the profile is for the White River or the Mowich Lake approach. The held Stephabegg 11,400 (White River) is within 3.5% but was excluded as the held page. Mountaineers also notes a carry-over: descent by the Emmons Glacier, needing a car shuttle from Mowich.

trailhead: Armstrong Pass trailhead (end of Willow Creek Road off Hwy 89)
note: Only round-trip figures: Gaia GPS gives 2,530 ft for a 9.3 mi out-and-back, and Summitborn gives ~2,700 ft for ~10 mi RT (an aggregator). Renotrails (held) is labelled an estimate. No one-way figure was stated.

trailhead: Meysan Lakes Trailhead (Whitney Portal Road)
note: Iron Hiker gives 6,000 ft for 13.7 mi round trip, via a SW chute rather than the NW slope. USFS gives only ~3,100 ft (another USFS PDF says 3,500) to Meysan Lake. The Backpacker page sits behind a login redirect. No one-way summit figure was found.

trailhead: Tuolumne Meadows / Lyell Canyon trailhead
note: Mountaineers gives 'a round trip of about 26 miles and 4000 feet elevation gain'. That scope is unclear, and 4,000 is less than the summit-minus-trailhead difference, so it is unusable. Summitborn (held) gives net gain only. No stated one-way figure.

trailhead: Whitney Portal (Mount Whitney Trail)
note: No page found states a one-way gain from Whitney Portal to Muir's summit. AllTrails and onX pages exist but showed no figures in the snippets; themtsarecalling covers a 5-day multi-peak trip. Summitborn (held) is the only figure.

trailhead: Whitney Portal
note: Hiking Project gives an out-and-back of 9.2 mi with ascent 5,928 and descent 5,919, and a high point of 14,292 (short of the summit), so the scope is unclear. Sayawe gives 6,000 ft together with 10.6 mi round trip. Neither labels a one-way gain. Powderproject mentions a winter road closure near 6,500 ft that adds a 3 mi road walk, an old note to recheck.

trailhead: Bunny Flat

evidence.fact: The climb from Bunny Flat ascends 5,400' over 4 1/2 miles, finishing up the Lightening Bolt Couloir.

note: Shasta Mountain Guides is a guide service, independent of Summitborn. 4.5 mi is the one-way Bunny Flat to summit distance, so 5,400 is the ascent. Its line is Anaconda Gulch, Hidden Valley, lower Cascade Gulch, then the couloir. TJ's Adventures gives 5,476 ft for 11.21 mi (round trip) by Cascade Gulch, not used.

trailhead: Lupine Meadows (via Garnet Canyon)
note: A DDG snippet from parkwolf.app said 'roughly a 6,000-foot climb', but the page now redirects to a list and could not be confirmed, so it is not evidence. Other pages give only the Garnet Canyon approach (~2,500-2,625 ft to Garnet Meadows). No stated one-way summit figure.

trailhead: Jenny Lake (boat dock on the west shore) / Jenny Lake Trailhead
note: CMC trip listing gives 8.0 mi and 4,000 ft as trip stats (Jenny Lake TH), not labelled one way. Summitborn (held) gives ~3,800 with the boat. Which start (boat or walking around the lake) changes the figure.

trailhead: Lupine Meadows Trailhead

evidence.fact: The East Face rises 5,600 ft directly above Lupine Meadows.
Teewinot Mountain from Lupine Meadows Trailhead: 8.3 mi Out/Back, Net gain 5,700 ft.

note: Both figures are NET vertical (summit above trailhead), not cumulative gain. They differ by 1.8%. The Wikipedia sentence matches SummitPost's wording. Stavislost is an independent GPS-track page.

trailhead: White River Campground / Glacier Basin Trailhead
note: The NPS Liberty Ridge route brief PDF had no readable text (WebFetch and Chrome both failed). IMG gives only ridge-base and Liberty Cap heights. The Mazamas page 403'd in WebFetch and was empty in Chrome. The held tahomawild/stephabegg figures are excluded, and Mountaineers gives segment gains only (summing them would be our math).

trailhead: Timberline Lodge

evidence.fact: Newton-Clark Headwall, Mount Hood: Vertical 1450' on headwall, 5649' to Timberline Lodge.

note: This is a ski-descent page, and the figure is net vertical from Timberline Lodge, not a cumulative ascent. Within 1.2% of the held 5,715 (wildsnow). Some parties start from Mt Hood Meadows (turns-all-year started at 5,400 ft), which would be a different trailhead.

trailhead: La Plata Peak / South Fork Lake Creek trailhead (Hwy 82)
note: Every page repeats 14ers.com's 5,900 with a round-trip length (Virtual Sherpa '5,900ft+' with 9.5-10+ RT). 14ers.com's route.php page has the same stat box. No independent one-way figure, and the ridge has significant up-and-down.

trailhead: Grays Peak Trailhead, Stevens Gulch (Bakerville exit 221)
note: USFS gives only an elevation range (11,241-14,272 ft). CFI 14ers.org gives no gain. Summitborn and SummitPost give round-trip-paired figures. A DDG snippet of the FDRD 'Grays Peak FDT 54' PDF reads 'Elevation Gain/Loss: +3,001 ft', but the PDF text could not be extracted, so it is not evidence. Re-check that PDF by eye. 14ers.com TH note (Jul 2026): people still park along the road before the trailhead despite signs.
